findings.title: Global view permission is treated as global group-management permission
findings.body: `canManage()` grants access when the caller has either `view` or `manage` on the all-groups resource. This method guards operations such as `POST /groups`, so an administrator assigned only the read-only `view` scope can create top-level groups. Restrict this evaluation to the `manage` scope; `view` should only be accepted by the view/list checks.

findings.title: Individually created group authorization resources are not assigned the Groups type
findings.body: Resources created by `getOrCreateResource` receive scopes but never have their type set to `resourceType`. `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` enumerates individual grants using `resourceStore.findByType(..., "Groups", ...)`, so resources created for individual groups are omitted from that enumeration. As a result, a `view-members` or `manage-members` grant on a specific group will not constrain user searches to that group's members. Set the resource type when creating schema resources (at least for the Groups resource type).

findings.title: Group-member search uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: The code passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission`, which looks up a resource by name, and then adds that same authorization-resource ID to the returned set. Schema resources are named with the Keycloak group ID, while their resource IDs are separately generated. Consequently the lookup misses the individual resource and the set later supplied to user queries contains IDs that do not identify any group, causing delegated group-member visibility/searches to return no matching users. Use `groupResource.getName()` for both the permission lookup and the returned group-ID set.

findings.title: Existing enabled admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with the Groups schema
findings.body: `init` returns immediately whenever an admin-permissions client already exists. Realms which enabled fine-grained admin permissions before this change therefore retain a resource server without the new Groups resource and its scopes. Creating or evaluating group scope permissions in those realms can fail because the scopes/resource cannot be found, and there is no migration path in this code to add them. Initialization must reconcile the existing resource server with newly introduced schema scopes and all-resource entries rather than returning unconditionally.
